discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of single spins in diamond (NV centres) and their use as quantum sensors
motivation: Wrachtrup and Jelezko first detected and coherently manipulated the spin of a single nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond, and kept it coherent at room temperature. This turned one electronic spin in a solid into a quantum system that can be addressed individually and read out optically. Lukin showed, in theory and in experiment, that such spins act as nanoscale magnetometers with quantum-limited sensitivity. Together they created NV quantum sensing, which now images magnetism in 2D materials, measures superconductivity at megabar pressures inside diamond anvil cells, detects nuclear magnetic resonance in nanolitre volumes, and maps neuronal and biological fields. It is also a leading platform for quantum networks and for loophole-free Bell tests. Few advances in quantum optics have given so many areas of physics a new, reliable, quantitative measuring tool. The work combines conceptual depth, the control of individual quantum systems, with broad practical impact.
